follow.send.summary: Email a sender a code so they can follow what they sent
follow.send.description: Use the follow token the send reply returned. Emails a 6-digit code, valid 10 minutes, to the address on that item; at most 3 codes an hour to one address. Solve the Holm challenge first.

follow.verify.description: Five tries per code. On success the item's email counts as the sender's: they get replies and see it under Your feedback when signed in with that address.

accounts.create.summary: Start a feedback project without an account
accounts.create.description: Solve the Holm challenge first (GET /_holm/challenge?operation=accounts.create, about 30 s in a browser, a few seconds in Python), then POST /api/accounts.create with Holm-Challenge and Holm-Challenge-Solution. Returns the project with its snippet and an API key shown once: store it with the app (a Holm outbound secret, or a gitignored .env), never print it. The key reaches only this project. Ten a minute from one address. Until someone keeps it, the project takes no files and 100 items a day, and it is deleted after 90 days unused.

projects.get.summary: Read a feedback form’s public settings
projects.get.description: Use a project id from an embed snippet to read the widget's appearance, kinds, contact rules, rating and questions before submitting. Never returns the owner, allowed sites or inbox.

feedback.submit.description: Submit JSON feedback to a widget project using its current form rules, allowed sites and hourly spam cap. Read projects_get first. Supply the source page url when sites are restricted, and reuse one Idempotency-Key only for retries of the same input. No attachments; use the existing multipart widget route for files.

projects.list.summary: List your projects and what’s waiting
projects.list.description: Call this first when signed in: it lists the projects the person owns, newest first, with each one’s id (for items_list, items_create and stats_get), name, whether it is for a site or a place, its public page if it has one, the sites its button is on, and how many new items and comments wait for them.

items.list.description: Use while signed in as the project’s owner; projects_list gives the project ids. Returns the newest items first, 100 by default (up to 1,000 with limit), including private contact details and file metadata. Optionally filter by open (new, planned or in progress), new, planned, progress, done or closed. Other people cannot read this inbox.

status.description: open, new, planned, progress, done or closed; leave out for all.

limit.description: How many items to return, newest first (default 100).

items.done.description: Use after resolving feedback while signed in as its project's owner. Changes only the status to done, records the same private thread event as dashboard triage, and returns the updated item. Optionally send an Idempotency-Key for safe retries.

items.create.summary: File an item, answer it and share it
items.create.description: Use while signed in as the project's owner for feedback that reached you another way, like a chat. Give a title (or a body whose first line is one); optionally the kind, who asked, their email (kept private and never emailed), a status, an answer posted as the project's public reply, and share: true for a link that opens the item and its answer with no sign-in. The item's share field is that link. Optionally send an Idempotency-Key for safe retries.

items.share.summary: Turn an item’s link on or off
items.share.description: Use while signed in as the item's project owner. share true gives the item a link that opens it and its approved comments with no sign-in (the same link if it has one), false stops the link at once, and "new" replaces it so the old one stops. The link never shows contact details, the page, browser, answers or files. Returns the item; its share field is the link or null.

itemId.description: The item id from items_list or items_create.

stats.get.summary: Read a project’s visits, scans and sends
stats.get.description: Use while signed in as the project's owner to inspect daily visits, QR scans, email visits, form opens, submissions, votes and comments, plus source pages, kinds and ratings. Choose 7, 30 or 90 days; the default is 30. Counts are events, not unique visitors.
